rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when someone or something is standing straight rather than bent or lying down.

example.english: Stand upright so you look more energetic in the photo.
example.traditional: 你企直啲，影相先精神㗎。
example.jyutping: nei5 kei5 zik6 di1 jing2 soeng2 sin1 zing1 san4 gaa3

rows.note: Use 直立 as the all-purpose physical term for something vertical or erect.

example.english: The tree remained upright after the heavy rain.
example.traditional: 場大雨之後，棵樹仲係直立喺度。
example.jyutping: coeng4 daai6 jyu5 zi1 hau6 fo2 syu6 zung6 hai6 zik6 lap6 hai2 dou6

rows.note: Use 擺正 when an object has been placed in its proper orientation rather than being overturned.

example.english: The chair was knocked over, so I put it upright again.
example.traditional: 張凳畀人撞跌咗，我幫你擺正返。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 dang3 bei2 jan4 zong6 dit3 zo2 ngo5 bong1 nei5 baai2 zing3 faan1

rows.note: Use this for being on one's feet, especially when contrasting standing with sitting or using a wheelchair.

example.english: They don't need a wheelchair now; they can still stay upright on their own.
example.traditional: 佢而家唔使坐輪椅，仲可以自己企住。
example.jyutping: keoi5 ji4 gaa1 m4 sai2 co5 leon4 ji2 zung6 ho2 ji5 zi6 gei2 kei5 zyu6

rows.note: Use 正派 for a person whose character and conduct are morally decent and trustworthy.

example.english: They are upright people, so you can trust them.
example.traditional: 佢哋個人好正派，做事好有交帶。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 go3 jan4 hou2 zing3 paai1 zou6 si6 hou2 jau5 gaau1 daai3
